question: Does the bare “Vinas” label in Quezon's historical flood advisory match the existing Viñas River lead?
purpose: Resolve a source-name/locality crosswalk while keeping the historical advisory separate from exact reach identity, river geometry, fish evidence, and current hazard status.

findings.evidence: Quezon Provincial Government General Flood Advisory No. 14, issued 7 August 2026, lists “Vinas” among Quezon rivers and tributaries likely to be affected by that forecast.

The official EMB CALABARZON Monitor (April-June 2005) names “Viñas River” with the parenthetical locality “Guinayangan-Tagkawayan, Quezon.” Its indexed text also reports a 2005 classification/public-hearing context; the PDF could not be directly retrieved in this review.
doesNotSupport: a fish survey or fish occurrence
a current classification or water-quality state

findings.evidence: The official 2025 NGA Sailing Directions independently names “Vinas River” near Guinayangan and describes a navigable entry and an approximately four-mile northwestward reach. The indexed route text is navigation context only; the PDF was too large for page-level review and the route was not digitized.
doesNotSupport: freshwater extent, fish evidence, or current access conditions

findings.evidence: DPWH Department Order No. 47, series of 2022, Annex D-2 lists a Region IV-A principal basin named “Vinas,” row 94, with a reported area of 159 sq km.

crosswalk.resolutionLevel: source-name and province/locality level; exact advisory reach and route unverified
crosswalk.confidence: The Quezon advisory's bare “Vinas” label matches the official EMB “Viñas River” spelling and Quezon locality context. NGA independently uses the unaccented “Vinas River” name near Guinayangan. DPWH provides same-name basin context but is not used to define the channel.
crosswalk.mergeDecision: Link the advisory label to the existing Viñas River research lead and do not create a duplicate lead. Keep the separate Hinabaan River lead unmerged: no reviewed source establishes that Viñas and Hinabaan are the same feature.

reuseAndLimitations: The EMB bulletin and NGA publication were reviewed through official indexed text; neither source's full underlying pages were directly examined during this crosswalk review.
The DPWH area is a principal-basin table value, not channel length, river boundary, or geometry.
No item-specific permission for structured public-app reuse was established; only short factual name/locality summaries are retained.
The August 2026 flood advisory is historical and is not current hazard guidance.
The name crosswalk does not establish fish presence or absence, current water quality, salinity, access, fishing legality, or safety.
nextActions: Seek permitted route-scale hydrography or an authoritative LGU/NAMRIA map to identify the exact advisory reach and channel route.
Keep the separate Hinabaan lead until a source explicitly crosswalks the two named features.
Search dated, station-resolved fish studies independently; do not derive fish claims from river names, basin areas, or navigation text.
